content.text: I've hit my search limit, so I'll open the Board's LCSW page to verify the entity rules.

In California, a licensed LCSW in her own private practice:

### 1. Professional corporation - YES, permitted

The Board of Behavioral Sciences states the LCSW private-practice definition as:

> “A “private practice” is a setting owned by a licensed clinical social worker, a licensed marriage and family therapist, a licensed psychologist, a licensed professional clinical counselor, or a licensed physician and surgeon, or a professional corporation of any of those licensed professions, as defined in section 13401(b) of the Corporations Code.”

The Board adds:

> “Note that professional corporations are included in the above definition .”

> “A professional corporation must register with the California Secretary of State and meet the requirements of the Corporations Code.”

> “It may be appropriate to include professional corporations in the definition of private practice, as a single licensee can form a professional corporation .”

Other sole-owner / multi-owner forms noted by the Board:

> “When owned by one licensee, it would be considered a sole proprietorship.”

> “However, when a practice is owned by two or more licensees, the company could be either a professional corporation or a partnership.”

The Board's current LCSW applicant page also lists as a setting category:

> “Private Practice and Professional Corporation Settings”

> “Registrants with a subsequent registration number cannot work in a private practice or a”

> “professional corporation setting. There are no exceptions.”

### 2. Ordinary LLC - NOT FOUND on the official pages reviewed

> It wasn't found - no sentence on the official Board pages opened for this answer expressly states whether a licensed LCSW may or may not use an ordinary LLC for private practice.

### 3. Professional LLC - NOT FOUND on the official pages reviewed

> It wasn't found - no sentence on the official Board pages opened for this answer expressly states whether California offers / permits a professional LLC for LCSW private practice, or whether she must use a professional corporation instead.

**Bottom line from official sources reviewed:** A professional corporation is expressly included as a permitted LCSW private-practice owner-entity. Whether an ordinary LLC or a professional LLC is permitted or prohibited was not stated on those official pages.
